title: EIP-8476: Permanent EOA Delegation Opt-Out
description: Allow EOAs to permanently disable delegation while retaining ordinary transaction origination.
author: nicolashw (@nicolashw) <nicolaspuran96@gmail.com>
bodyPreview: ## Abstract Allow an externally owned account (EOA) to permanently disable [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) delegation by installing an account-code marker that consensus rules recognize but the EVM observes as empty code. A narrowly defined, previously invalid form of a set-code transaction performs the opt-out. The account keeps its address and continues to behave as an ordinary EOA at the EVM level, but no subsequent delegation authorization can replace or clear the marker. ## Motivation [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) gives EOAs a persistent capability to delegate execution. Some accounts, including institutional wallets, exchange hot wallets, and treasuries, do not need this capability. Their operational controls may include withdrawal approvals, frequency and amount limits, monitoring, and emergency suspension outside Ethereum consensus. Delegated execution can invalidate assumptions behind those controls and compress the time available for intervention. An account owner should be able to eliminate this capability explicitly. This proposal only removes delegation: a compromised private key can still sign ordinary transactions, transfer funds, and authorize actions in contracts. It does not enforce withdrawal delays or replace key management and operational controls. ## Specification The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174). Except for the changes below, EIP-7702 and ordinary transaction and EVM rules are unchanged. Here, `sender` is the address recovered from the outer transaction signature; `authority` is the address recovered from an authorization signature. `||` denotes byte concatenation. ### Parameters and Account State | Parameter | Proposed value | | --- | --- | | `OPT_OUT_CODE` | `0xef0200` (exactly 3 bytes) | | `OPT_OUT_STATE_BYTES` | `3` | `OPT_OUT_CODE` is a candidate encoding for this draft, not an assigned code format. Its allocation requires coordination before this proposal can become final; the namespace concern is described in Rationale. All byte comparisons below use this exact candidate value. An account is delegation-disabled if and only if its raw stored code equals `OPT_OUT_CODE`. Clients MUST check the complete code, including its length; a prefix match is insufficient. This marker is not the 23-byte EIP-7702 delegation indicator `0xef0100 || address` and MUST NOT be parsed as one. The account's state-trie `codeHash` MUST be `keccak256(OPT_OUT_CODE)` (`0x804e3605b87cf0b8b9e86c36d895f477b73bafa75f854f0a2b17712a5c88c2e9` for the candidate bytes), not the literal marker bytes and not the empty-code hash. No storage slot or additional account field is introduced. [EIP-3541](./eip-3541.md) continues to prohibit installing code beginning with `0xef` through contract creation. ### Opt-Out Transaction Extend the validity rules for EIP-7702 set-code transactions (`TransactionType = 0x04`). An empty `authorization_list`, previously always invalid, MUST be accepted only when all of these conditions hold: - `destination == sender`; - `value == 0`; - `data` is the empty byte string; - `access_list` is the empty list. This form is an opt-out transaction. Every other set-code transaction with an empty authorization list MUST remain invalid. A non-empty authorization list retains its existing meaning, including when its other fields match the conditions above. The transaction uses the existing set-code RLP envelope and signature scheme. Explicitly, its signature is over: ```text keccak256(0x04 || rlp([chain_id, nonce, max_priority_fee_per_gas, max_fee_per_gas, gas_limit, sender, 0, empty_bytes, [], []])) ``` The signature fields are appended to these unsigned fields as in EIP-7702. There is no new transaction type, authorization signature domain, sentinel delegation address, or relayed opt-out authorization. The outer transaction's chain ID MUST equal the current chain ID under the existing typed-transaction rules. The chain-agnostic `chain_id = 0` exception for EIP-7702 authorization tuples does not apply to this operation. A chain whose own ID is zero still uses its ordinary outer transaction rules. Existing signature, nonce, fee, balance, block-gas and transaction-gas validity checks apply, with the sender-code exception below. In particular, [EIP-2681](./eip-2681.md) requires `nonce < 2**64 - 1`. Gas accounting follows [EIP-2780](./eip-2780.md) and [EIP-8037](./eip-8037.md). The intrinsic gas of an opt-out transaction is `TX_BASE_COST` execution gas, as for a zero-value transaction to self; it has no recipient-access, value, calldata, or authorization charges. A gas limit below the intrinsic gas MUST make the transaction invalid. In the pre-execution phase defined by EIP-2780, if the sender's code at transaction start is empty, the transaction MUST charge `OPT_OUT_STATE_BYTES × CPSB` state gas for the stored marker. No state gas is charged when the sender's code at transaction start is an EIP-7702 delegation indicator or already `OPT_OUT_CODE`, consistent with EIP-2780's treatment of an indicator present at transaction start. No account-creation charge applies, because the sender necessarily exists. If this charge cannot be paid, the transaction remains valid and is included; the nonce increment and fee payment persist, the marker is not installed, and the receipt status is `0`, following EIP-2780's pre-execution out-of-gas rule. Fee purchase, unused-gas return, base-fee burning, and priority-fee payment follow [EIP-1559](./eip-1559.md). No gas refund is generated by replacing an existing delegation or repeating the operation. After validating the transaction, clients MUST perform the ordinary sender nonce increment and fee accounting and set the sender's code to `OPT_OUT_CODE`. The transaction MUST NOT execute EVM code,
